messages:
olivia (AM): Heads-up: new enterprise prospect (bank) / sealed-network POC. Security team wants explicit chain-of-custody for sneakernet deliveries, signed SBOMs, per-delivery acceptance checklist, and a pricing line for physical courier. Also asked about rollback parity between full vs delta bundles. Can we outline operational constraints and costs?

sam (Solutions): Short: yes we can support. Key choices to present: full signed bundle vs signed delta. For courier flows we hand off an integrity-checked tarball + signature + SBOM. Two customer-acceptable handoff patterns: (A) single signed artifact on USB/SSD sealed bag, or (B) manifest + chunked archive pieces (for >1TB transfer).

ash (Eng): Runtime constraints:
- Full-bundle: guaranteed atomic apply if bundle verified; simpler rollback because previous snapshot retained.
- Delta-bundle: smaller transfer, but patch agent must perform binary diffs; requires KV-cache compatibility and explicit migration steps. If migration fails, rollback may need a full-bundle restore, which costs time.
- Recommendation: for any model weight changes use full-bundle. Use delta for config/runtime patches only.

olivia (AM): They explicitly require signed SBOM (CycloneDX) and a human-readable vuln summary included with the bundle. Can we automate per-delivery signing?

packaging-bot: Automation status: CI can produce sbom.cdx.json and run distro/CVE scan. We can produce per-build SBOM signatures (sig-sbom.pem) and include an immutable manifest with SHA256 checksums.

mike (Legal): Contract notes: require attestation of integrity at handoff (signed manifest + courier chain-of-custody form). Add clause limiting our liability for customer-side mishandling after confirmed delivery. Also export-control clause if models are restricted.

sam (Solutions): Pricing & ops: propose three charge components for POC:
1) Onboarding engineering fee (one-time) to wire bundle signing, courier automation, and runbook: recommended $8k flat for a standard POC; up to $18k for complex delta tooling.
2) Per-delivery physical courier fee: we bill actual courier + handling (min $450 per sealed delivery inside NA).
3) Extended POC dedication: if they want reserved node(s) for the POC we can prorate Dedicated list price at 40%/month for POC length; or a flat weekly commitment + pro-rated charge.

olivia (AM): Customer wants a 90-day POC, two deliveries (initial + fortnightly patches). How to price delivery cadence?

sam (Solutions): If fortnightly infra-only patches are delivered by sneakernet, include courier fee per delivery. For delta patching we can bundle multiple deltas into a single physical delivery to reduce cost. Suggest offering a bundled courier discount: after 3 deliveries within the POC, apply a 20% handling credit.

ash (Eng): Operationally we recommend this flow in runbook:
1) Pre-sign and immutably store artifacts in our CI.
2) Produce manifest with per-file SHA256, SBOM hash, and signature.
3) Hand off to approved courier who collects a signed receipt (chain-of-custody).
4) Customer verifies signature locally and runs verify/prefetch before apply.
Commands (copy into one-pager):
```
# verify artifact
redwoodctl verify --manifest ./manifest.json --pubkey /etc/redwood/pubkey.pem
# prefetch
redwoodctl prefetch --bundle ./bundle.tar.gz
# apply (atomic)
redwoodctl apply --bundle ./bundle.tar.gz --backup /var/backups/redwood-prev.tar.gz
# rollback if needed
redwoodctl rollback --snapshot /var/backups/redwood-prev.tar.gz
```
Note: delta-apply has an extra `redwoodctl patch-apply` step and requires patch-agent v1.2+.

olivia (AM): They want downtime guarantees. Can we give numbers?

sam (Solutions): For infra/config only patches on a multi-node POC cluster, we target rolling apply with <3 minutes of impact. For single-node or model-weight swap full-bundle: expect a maintenance window ~30 minutes depending on model size and disk I/O. Always advise prefetch + cache warm to shrink window. We'll document expected times per model size in the runbook.

mike (Legal): Add telemetry assurance: the customer requires no outbound telemetry by default. We'll include an opt-in for any telemetry with explicit customer enable. Also require signed acceptance after install (a one-line acceptance record recorded in the delivery manifest).

olivia (AM): Security team also wants an acceptance checklist they can sign on receipt. Items: physical seals intact, signature verification OK, SBOM present, checksums match, CVE summary reviewed, and media sanitized after ingestion. Can we produce that?

packaging-bot: Checklist template ready; will include signature verification steps and a media-sanitization note (shred/crypto-erase).

sam (Solutions): Risk notes:
- Deltas introduce more operational blast radius for cache/kv mismatches. Plan for a fallback boxed full-bundle on a second disk if delta apply fails.
- For emergency hotfixes we can provision a same-day courier in-region for an extra fee (SLA + premium courier cost).

olivia (AM): Action items & dates:
- ash: produce sealed one-page runbook + courier checklist + SBOM sample by Fri (1779150000)
- sam: pricing sheet with onboarding fee tiers + per-delivery handling fee + 90-day POC invoice example by Thu (1779135000)
- mike: SOW redlines (liability carveouts, telemetry opt-out, export check, chain-of-custody clause) by Mon (1779200000)
- packaging-bot: attach checklist template to the runbook.

ash (Eng): Ack. I'll include a table: full-bundle vs delta (size, downtime, rollback complexity).

sam (Solutions): Ack. I'll include a courier cost sensitivity table and an option for customer-provided courier (we then just sign manifest).

olivia (AM): Great. I'll share the proposed commercial & ops plan with the customer once we have the runbook and pricing. Thanks.

ops-bot: Reminder: create sealed-deploy runbook entry in repo and label telemetry opt-out as default for sealed networks. Follow-up scheduled for 1779136000.
